resume.skillManagerTitle: Skill Manager - AI Agent Skill Management Tool
resume.skillManagerMeta: 2026.10 - 2026.11 | Personal project - Requirements design and development
resume.skillManagerBackground: Built a unified content library and multi-entry management tool to address scattered, duplicated, and conflicting Skill configurations across multiple AI coding tools.
resume.skillManager1Body: Mapped user journeys and feature boundaries, and organized 56 user stories and 168 acceptance scenarios into an SRS and story map so requirements are traceable and results verifiable.
resume.skillManager2Body: Implemented an application service shared by CLI, Web, and MCP entry points, giving users and agents consistent management, search, and read interfaces.
resume.skillManager3Body: Implemented snapshots, digest verification, and idempotent handling of repeated imports; separated content results from index results and added status queries and rebuild entry points to locate partial failures.
resume.voiceTitle: Voice AI Front Desk - AI Voice Intent Screening System
resume.voiceMeta: 2026.08 - Present | Seattle startup collaboration project - Backend development
resume.voiceBackground: Built an AI voice backend for real-estate seller intent screening, handling external call creation, result association, and recovery from unknown outcomes.
resume.voice1Body: Implemented the voice service adapter, persisting request snapshots and idempotency keys before dispatch, and controlling concurrent sends with atomic database claims and leases.
resume.voice2Body: Applied bounded recovery and status queries to unknown outcomes such as lost responses and failed local saves, limiting the risk of duplicate creation and incorrect association.
resume.voice3Body: Verified recovery paths against real PostgreSQL with a two-process restart scenario and kept failure-handling and verification records; results are limited to local engineering verification, and real calls and deployment have not yet been accepted.
resume.smartchainTitle: SmartChain Core - Go / QUIC Communication and Protocol Foundation
resume.smartchainMeta: 2026.06 - 2026.08 | New York startup collaboration project - Go backend development
resume.smartchainBackground: Strengthened the communication and protocol foundation for a startup collaboration project, addressing contract drift, response correlation, and blocking on silent peers.
resume.smartchain1Body: Fixed validation of protocol identifiers, UTF-8, length, and trailing JSON data; implemented response correlation and fixed error messages to reject malformed messages without leaking parsing details.
resume.smartchain2Body: Added per-read and per-write timeouts on QUIC streams and handled context cancellation, cleaning up streams by failure stage so blocked requests can exit while the underlying connection stays reusable.
resume.smartchain3Body: Added tests for agent registration conflicts, timeouts, and cancellation, and synced architecture and verification docs; 2 of my PRs were merged into the development line as milestone component work.
resume.medmemoTitle: MedMemo - AI Health Information and Memory Desktop App

resume.medmemo1Body: Connected the Go backend and React frontend through Wails, integrating model APIs and SSE streaming output to support continuous AI conversations.
resume.medmemo2Body: Implemented hybrid vector and keyword retrieval with candidate reranking; when the vector service is unavailable, keyword results are kept so knowledge queries still work.
resume.medmemo3Body: Implemented conversation memory, history compression, and summarization strategies, added automated tests, and fixed Windows DLL lookup and CI packaging issues.
resume.jobcopilotMeta: 2026.01 - 2026.05 | Major contributor and maintainer, open-source project
resume.jobcopilotBackground: Contributed to an AI job-search platform, improving features and stability around cross-page chat, long-context handling, and resume editing.
resume.jobcopilot1Body: Implemented a Copilot drawer and shared state, adding the chat entry to the main layout so different pages reuse the same chat component.
resume.jobcopilot2Body: Contributed to token usage tracking, window configuration, and RabbitMQ-based async compression, using prompts to constrain summary facts and format and reusing history summaries in later requests.
resume.jobcopilot3Body: Used Spring transaction synchronization callbacks to defer vector generation to afterCommit, moving embedding work out of the resume-edit transaction.
resume.skill1Body: Project experience with Java / Spring Boot, Python / FastAPI, and Go, covering REST APIs, database access, async tasks, and service integration; connected frontend and backend features with React / TypeScript and Wails.
resume.skill2Body: LLM API integration, prompt design, RAG, hybrid vector and keyword retrieval, and SSE streaming; implemented conversation memory, summarization, and context compression, and used MCP to expose tools to agents.
resume.skill3Body: Used PostgreSQL / pgvector and SQLite / sqlite-vec for business data and vector search; experience with SQL, transaction boundaries, retrieval fallback, and index-state troubleshooting; exposure to Redis caching and RabbitMQ messaging.
resume.skill4Body: Idempotent deduplication, atomic claims, leases, bounded recovery, and state reconciliation; experience with Go / QUIC protocol validation, request-response correlation, stream timeouts, and context cancellation.
resume.skill5Body: Git, Linux, Docker Compose, and GitHub Actions; wrote unit, integration, and failure regression tests; experience with automated lab-environment deployment, Windows build troubleshooting, and Codex-assisted development; able to write SRS documents, user stories, and acceptance criteria.

medmemo.title: Desktop AI Chat and Health Memory Application
medmemo.kicker: Built MedMemo with Go, Wails, and React/TypeScript to combine AI conversations, health records, and memory retrieval in a desktop application.
medmemo.caption: Go backend, React/TypeScript interface, conversational memory, and model integration.
medmemo.memoryBody: Working, short-term, and long-term memory layers.
medmemo.licenseBody: Open-source software under the MIT license.
medmemo.takeawayTitle: Connected chat, memory, and desktop workflows
medmemo.takeawayBody: As the primary developer, built the Go backend and React interface, integrated model providers and memory retrieval, and worked on testing and desktop packaging.
medmemo.feature1Body: Integrated SQLite/SQLCipher and local retrieval components to store conversations and retrieve relevant health information.
medmemo.feature2Body: Implemented working, short-term, and long-term memory with vector and keyword search so earlier information can be recalled during later conversations.
medmemo.feature3Body: Integrated OpenAI-compatible APIs and local model providers with streaming responses and summary compression to manage conversation context.
medmemo.feature4Body: Added memory and privacy workflow tests and fixed Windows library packaging and CI configuration to support repeatable builds.
medmemo.proofTitle: Go application layers and replaceable integrations
medmemo.proofIntro: Organized domain logic, use cases, repository interfaces, and model adapters with Clean Architecture and Google Wire.
medmemo.stack1Body: Wails, Go, React, TypeScript, Zustand, and desktop packaging.
medmemo.stack2Body: Clean Architecture, Google Wire, domain entities, use cases, repositories, and adapters.
medmemo.stack3Body: Model providers, ONNX Runtime, embeddings, sqlite-vec, and memory retrieval.
medmemo.safetyBody: MedMemo is a health information management and consultation-assistance tool. It is not a medical device and does not provide diagnosis, treatment, prescriptions, or medical decisions.
medmemo.stackBody: Go backend and React/TypeScript interface connected through Wails bindings.
medmemo.desktopBody: Desktop application framework and build tooling.

jobcopilot.title: AI Resume Processing and Job Matching Platform
jobcopilot.kicker: Contributed to a React, Spring Boot, and FastAPI platform connecting resume processing, semantic matching, AI chat, and application tracking.
jobcopilot.caption: Semantic retrieval, asynchronous AI workflows, and containerized services.
jobcopilot.runtimeBody: Main application runtimes: React frontend, Spring Boot backend, and Python AI service.
jobcopilot.vectorBody: Semantic search foundation for resume and job matching.
jobcopilot.licenseBody: Open-source software under the MIT license.
jobcopilot.takeawayTitle: Connected resume data with AI workflows
jobcopilot.takeawayBody: As a major contributor and maintainer, developed backend and AI service integrations for resume processing, job matching, chat, and application tracking.
jobcopilot.feature1Body: Connected upload, parsing, versioning, editing, and export through REST APIs so resume content can move between the interface and AI services.
jobcopilot.feature2Body: Integrated PostgreSQL/pgvector retrieval to compare resume content with job descriptions and support AI-assisted matching.
jobcopilot.feature3Body: Used RabbitMQ workers and Redis coordination to separate long-running AI tasks from user-facing API workflows.
jobcopilot.feature4Body: Supported Docker Compose and Nginx configuration to connect the frontend, backend, AI services, database, cache, and queue through a shared gateway.
jobcopilot.proofTitle: Backend domains and AI service boundaries
jobcopilot.proofIntro: Worked with domain-driven backend modules, REST interfaces, message queues, and vector storage to connect application workflows with AI services.
jobcopilot.stack1Body: React, TypeScript, Nginx, multilingual interfaces, authentication, resume management, chat, and application tracking.
jobcopilot.stack2Body: Java 25, Spring Boot, DDD, hexagonal architecture, Maven modules, REST controllers, and application services.
jobcopilot.stack3Body: Python, FastAPI, LiteLLM, embeddings, resume/job parsing, RabbitMQ consumers, Redis, and MinIO model artifacts.
jobcopilot.stackBody: Java/Spring Boot backend and Python/FastAPI AI services.
jobcopilot.resultBody: Fixed resume editing by triggering vector generation after the database transaction commits, keeping external AI calls outside the transaction boundary.
